**2. SITE DESCRIPTIONS**

**2.1 Site A – Corporate Headquarters & Primary Manufacturing Plant (Pune, Maharashtra)**

Site A is the largest facility, comprising a 12,000 sq.m. manufacturing floor, a three-storey administrative block, and a central utilities building. The site operates two shifts (06:00–22:00) six days per week. Major energy-consuming equipment includes two 350 TR centrifugal chillers (Chiller 1 and Chiller 2), eight air handling units, and a 500 kVA transformer serving the production load. The chiller plant operates year-round due to process cooling requirements.

**2.2 Site B – Regional Distribution Centre (Nagpur, Maharashtra)**

Site B is a 6,500 sq.m. warehousing and logistics hub, operating on a single shift (08:00–18:00) five days per week. Energy consumption is dominated by lighting (60%), material handling equipment charging, and a small HVAC system for the office area. The site has a 250 kVA transformer. The compressed air system, used for packaging equipment, has been identified as a significant area of energy loss.

**2.3 Site C – Component Fabrication Unit (Aurangabad, Maharashtra)**

Site C is a 4,200 sq.m. fabrication unit producing metal components. It operates two shifts (07:00–23:00) six days per week. Energy use is primarily driven by electric arc welding, CNC machinery, and an ageing air compressor. The site has a 315 kVA transformer. Power quality issues, particularly low power factor, have been noted in preliminary assessments.

**4.5 Site C – Variable Frequency Drives (VFD) on Pumping Systems**

The Site C pumping system comprises three sets of pumps serving the cooling tower, process water, and utility water circuits. The existing control method uses throttling valves to regulate flow, which wastes energy because the pumps run at constant speed even when demand is lower.

| Pump Set | Rated Power (kW) | Present Avg. Load (kW) | Est. Load with VFD (kW) | Annual Savings (kWh) |
|----------|------------------|------------------------|-------------------------|----------------------|
| Cooling tower pumps (2 no.) | 22 each | 31.5 (combined) | 19.8 (combined) | 60,840 |
| Process water pumps (3 no.) | 18.5 each | 41.2 (combined) | 27.6 (combined) | 70,720 |
| Utility water pump (1 no.) | 15 | 11.4 | 8.9 | 13,000 |

The above savings are calculated for 5,200 operating hours per year, with the VFD operating at an average speed reduction of 15–20% compared to full speed. A detailed measurement of the flow and pressure was done during the audit visit using a portable ultrasonic flow meter and the plant's existing pressure gauges.

Total estimated annual energy savings: 144,560 kWh
Cost of electricity (average, including demand charges): INR 8.40 per kWh
Annual cost savings: INR 1,214,304

Implementation cost (VFDs, bypass starters, control wiring, installation, and commissioning):
- Cooling tower pumps: INR 420,000
- Process water pumps: INR 540,000
- Utility water pump: INR 165,000
- Total: INR 1,125,000

Simple payback period: 0.93 years (approximately 11 months)

It is recommended that the VFDs be installed with manual bypass starters so that the pumps can continue to operate at full speed if a VFD fails. The existing throttling valves should be retained in the line but opened fully during VFD operation to avoid unnecessary pressure drop.

documents.title: Energy Audit Report – DEFG Facilities – 2024
documents.content:
---

**2. SITE DESCRIPTIONS**

**2.1 Site A – Corporate Headquarters & Primary Manufacturing Plant (Pune, Maharashtra)**

Site A is the largest facility, comprising a 12,000 sq.m. manufacturing floor, a three-storey administrative block, and a central utilities building. The site operates two shifts (06:00–22:00) six days per week. Major energy-consuming equipment includes two 350 TR centrifugal chillers (Chiller 1 and Chiller 2), eight air handling units, and a 500 kVA transformer serving the production load. The chiller plant operates year-round due to process cooling requirements.

**2.2 Site B – Regional Distribution Centre (Nagpur, Maharashtra)**

Site B is a 6,500 sq.m. warehousing and logistics hub, operating on a single shift (08:00–18:00) five days per week. Energy consumption is dominated by lighting (60%), material handling equipment charging, and a small HVAC system for the office area. The site has a 250 kVA transformer. The compressed air system, used for packaging equipment, has been identified as a significant area of energy loss.

**2.3 Site C – Component Fabrication Unit (Aurangabad, Maharashtra)**

Site C is a 4,200 sq.m. fabrication unit producing metal components. It operates two shifts (07:00–23:00) six days per week. Energy use is primarily driven by electric arc welding, CNC machinery, and an ageing air compressor. The site has a 315 kVA transformer. Power quality issues, particularly low power factor, have been noted in preliminary assessments.

---

**3. ENERGY CONSUMPTION DATA**

The energy audit report states VFD Retrofit achieves energy_savings_percent of 18.5 percent. Record status: current.

The following tables present baseline energy consumption data recorded during the audit period. All data was collected via installed sub-meters, utility bills, and portable logging equipment. Consumption figures have been normalised for weather variations and production output where applicable.

**3.1 Monthly Electricity Consumption (kWh)**

**3.2 Peak Demand (kVA)**

Site C exceeded its contracted demand in February and March, incurring penalty charges of INR 18,400 and INR 22,100 respectively. This is attributed to the simultaneous operation of welding machines and the air compressor during shift changeover periods.

**3.3 Energy Performance Indicators (kWh per unit of production)**

Site B operates a 75 kW rotary screw air compressor supplying compressed air to the packaging and material handling areas. Leakage testing conducted using ultrasonic leak detectors during the audit identified 14 significant leak points across the distribution network. The estimated total leakage rate was measured at approximately 18% of the compressor’s rated output.

| Leak Location | Estimated Leakage (l/min) |
|---------------|---------------------------|
| Packaging line – coupling | 45 |
| Conveyor area – fitting | 38 |
| Pallet wrapper – hose | 52 |
| Maintenance bay – valve | 41 |
| Warehouse – pipe joint | 33 |
| Other locations (9 points) | 187 |
| **Total** | **396** |

Annual energy loss: 24.6 kW × 6,500 h × 0.70 = 111,930 kWh
Annual cost savings potential: 111,930 × INR 7.95 = INR 889,844

Estimated cost of repairs (replacement of fittings, hoses, and valves): INR 145,000
Simple payback period: 0.16 years (approximately 2 months)

It is strongly recommended that a routine leak detection and repair programme be established, with quarterly ultrasonic surveys and immediate tagging of identified leaks. Operator training on proper coupling and hose handling practices should also be provided to prevent recurrence.

**4.3 Site C – Waste Heat Recovery from Compressor Cooling System**

The compressor operates for approximately 5,200 hours per year with a load factor of 75%. The heat recovery unit (HRU) proposed for installation is a shell-and-tube type heat exchanger designed to capture heat from the cooling water circuit.

The audit report specifies Heat Recovery Unit with heat_recovery_capacity_kW of 120 kW. Record status: current.

This rating is based on the compressor’s average heat rejection rate at the observed operating conditions and is considered conservative, accounting for part-load operation and seasonal variations in cooling water inlet temperature.

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Heat recovery capacity | 120 kW |
| Annual operating hours | 5,200 |
| Heat recovery efficiency (estimated) | 85% |
| Useful heat recovered per year | 530,400 kWh (thermal) |
| Boiler efficiency (existing) | 82% |
| Equivalent fuel savings (furnace oil) | 48,200 litres/year |
| Cost of furnace oil | INR 62.50 per litre |
| Annual cost savings | INR 3,012,500 |

Estimated implementation cost (heat exchanger, piping, insulation, controls, installation): INR 2,450,000
Simple payback period: 0.81 years (approximately 10 months)

The recovered heat will raise the boiler feed water temperature from approximately 28°C to 65°C, reducing the thermal load on the boiler and correspondingly reducing furnace oil consumption. The HRU is designed with a bypass arrangement to allow continued compressor operation in the event of maintenance on the heat recovery circuit.

It should be noted that the recovered heat quantity is sufficient to meet approximately 62% of the total thermal energy demand of the phosphating line during winter months, with the balance supplied by the existing boiler. During summer months, when feed water temperature is higher, the recovered heat will be proportionally lower, but the system will continue to provide significant savings.

**4.4 Site C – Peak Demand Management**

documents.content:
**4.5 Site C – Variable Frequency Drives (VFD) on Pumping Systems**

The Site C pumping system comprises three sets of pumps serving the cooling tower, process water, and utility water circuits. The existing control method uses throttling valves to regulate flow, which wastes energy because the pumps run at constant speed even when demand is lower.

| Pump Set | Rated Power (kW) | Present Avg. Load (kW) | Est. Load with VFD (kW) | Annual Savings (kWh) |
|----------|------------------|------------------------|-------------------------|----------------------|
| Cooling tower pumps (2 no.) | 22 each | 31.5 (combined) | 19.8 (combined) | 60,840 |
| Process water pumps (3 no.) | 18.5 each | 41.2 (combined) | 27.6 (combined) | 70,720 |
| Utility water pump (1 no.) | 15 | 11.4 | 8.9 | 13,000 |

The above savings are calculated for 5,200 operating hours per year, with the VFD operating at an average speed reduction of 15–20% compared to full speed. A detailed measurement of the flow and pressure was done during the audit visit using a portable ultrasonic flow meter and the plant's existing pressure gauges.

Total estimated annual energy savings: 144,560 kWh
Cost of electricity (average, including demand charges): INR 8.40 per kWh
Annual cost savings: INR 1,214,304

Implementation cost (VFDs, bypass starters, control wiring, installation, and commissioning):
- Cooling tower pumps: INR 420,000
- Process water pumps: INR 540,000
- Utility water pump: INR 165,000
- Total: INR 1,125,000

Simple payback period: 0.93 years (approximately 11 months)

It is recommended that the VFDs be installed with manual bypass starters so that the pumps can continue to operate at full speed if a VFD fails. The existing throttling valves should be retained in the line but opened fully during VFD operation to avoid unnecessary pressure drop.

**4.6 Site C – Lighting System Upgrade**

The lighting survey covered all production halls, warehouses, office areas, and external lighting at Site C. The existing lighting comprises mostly 400W HPSV (high pressure sodium vapour) fixtures in the production halls and warehouses, with a mix of CFL and older T8 fluorescent tubes in office and utility areas.

| Area | Existing Fixture | Quantity | Proposed Fixture | Annual Savings (kWh) |
|------|------------------|----------|------------------|----------------------|
| Production Hall 1 | 400W HPSV | 120 | 200W LED high bay | 96,000 |
| Production Hall 2 | 400W HPSV | 85 | 200W LED high bay | 68,000 |
| Warehouse A | 250W HPSV | 40 | 120W LED high bay | 20,800 |
| Warehouse B | 250W HPSV | 32 | 120W LED high bay | 16,640 |
| Office block | T8 2×36W | 210 | LED 2×18W | 27,216 |
| External lighting | 150W HPSV | 25 | 60W LED street light | 9,750 |

The above savings assume 3,500 operating hours per year for indoor lighting and 4,200 hours for external lighting. The LED fixtures also have lower maintenance costs due to longer life, though these savings are not included in the payback calculation below.

Total annual energy savings: 238,406 kWh
Annual cost savings: INR 2,002,610

Implementation cost (fixtures, drivers, mounting accessories, installation, and disposal of old lamps):
- Indoor LED high bay fixtures: INR 1,150,000
- Office LED tube retrofits: INR 126,000
- External LED street lights: INR 87,500
- Total: INR 1,363,500

Simple payback period: 0.68 years (approximately 8 months)

The proposed LED fixtures have a colour temperature of 6500K for production areas and 4000K for office areas. Sample fixtures were installed in a 10-fixture trial in Production Hall 1 for two weeks during the audit, and lux measurements confirmed that the LED fixtures provide equal or better illumination levels compared to the existing HPSV fixtures. The trial was done in the first week of March 2024 and the results were recorded in Annexure C.
